children.text: pāpaṃ na kuryān manasā na vācā kāyena vā kiṃcana sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: One should not commit sin by mind, by speech, or by body — nothing whatsoever in the entire world;

children.text: riktaḥ kāmaiḥ smṛtimān saṃprajānaṃ duḥkhaṃ na seveta anarthasaṃhitam // Śag_1.1
children.translated_text: empty of sense-desires, mindful, clearly comprehending, one should not pursue suffering that is devoid of purpose. // <s>Śag</s> 1.1

children.text: ākhyeyasaṃjñinaḥ satvā ākhyeye 'smin pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beings who perceive in terms of the nameable are established in this nameable [world];

children.text: ākhyeyam aparijñāya yogam āyānti mṛtyunaḥ // Śag_2.1
children.translated_text: not fully comprehending the nameable, they come under the yoke of death. // <s>Śag</s> 2.1

children.text: ākhyeyaṃ tu parijñāya ākhyātāraṃ na manyate /
children.translated_text: But having fully comprehended the nameable, one does not conceive of a namer;

children.text: tad vai na vidyate tasya vadeyur yena taṃ pare // Śag_2.2
children.translated_text: indeed, that [basis] does not exist for such a one, by which others could speak of him. // <s>Śag</s> 2.2

children.text: samo viśeṣa uta vāpi hīno yo manyate sa vivadeta tena /
children.translated_text: Whoever thinks 'I am equal,' 'superior,' or 'inferior' — he would dispute on that account;

children.text: vidhātraye 'smin na vikampate yaḥ samo viśiṣṭaś ca na tasya bhavati // Śag_2.3
children.translated_text: one who is not shaken by these three modes of conceiving — for him there is neither 'equal' nor 'superior.' // <s>Śag</s> 2.3

children.text: ācchidya tṛṣṇām iha nāmarūpe prahāya mānaṃ ca na saṃgam eti /
children.translated_text: Having cut off craving here for name-and-form, having abandoned conceit, one does not become attached;

children.text: taṃ śāntadhūmam anighaṃ nirāśaṃ nādrākṣus te devamanuṣyaloke /
children.translated_text: him — whose fire is quenched, who is without affliction, without longing — they did not find in the world of <s>devas</s> and humans,

children.text: iha bāhirataś ca // Śag_2.4
children.translated_text: here or beyond. // <s>Śag</s> 2.4

children.text: kāmarāgābhibhūtatvāc cittaṃ me paridahyate /
children.translated_text: Overpowered by passion and desire, my mind is burning;

children.text: aṃga me gautama brūhi śāntiṃ tvam anukaṃpayā // Śag_3.1
children.translated_text: pray tell me, O <s>Gautama</s>, out of compassion, the way to peace. // <s>Śag</s> 3.1

children.text: viparyāsena saṃjñānāṃ cittaṃ te paridahyate /
children.translated_text: Through the distortion of your perceptions, your mind is burning;

children.text: nimittaṃ varjyatāṃ tasmāc chubhaṃ rāgopasaṃhitaṃ // Śag_3.2
children.translated_text: therefore, avoid the sign (<s>nimitta</s>) that is pleasant, connected with passion. // <s>Śag</s> 3.2

children.text: aśubhāṃ bhāvaya sadā tvam ekāgraḥ susamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Cultivate the unpleasant (<s>aśubhā</s>) always, with one-pointed mind, well-concentrated;

children.text: nirvāpayāśu rāgāgniṃ dahyase mā punaḥ punaḥ // Śag_3.3
children.translated_text: quickly extinguish the fire of passion — do not be burned again and again. // <s>Śag</s> 3.3

children.text: saṃskārāvaratāṃ paśya duḥkhato 'nātmatas tathā /
children.translated_text: See formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) as subject to cessation, as suffering, and as not-self;

children.text: smṛtiṃ kāyagatāṃ kṛtvā nirvedabahulo bhava // Śag_3.4
children.translated_text: having established mindfulness directed toward the body, become full of disenchantment (<s>nirveda</s>). // <s>Śag</s> 3.4

children.text: bhāvyatām animittaṃ ca mānānuśayanāśanaṃ /
children.translated_text: Cultivate the signless (<s>animitta</s>), which destroys the latent tendency of conceit (<s>māna</s>);

children.text: tato mānābhisamayād duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyasi // Śag_3.5
children.translated_text: then, through the breaking through of conceit, you will make an end of suffering. // <s>Śag</s> 3.5

children.text: kumārikāpraśnagāthā:
children.translated_text: Verses of the Maiden's Questions (<s>Kumārikāpraśnagāthā</s>):

children.text: kathaṃvihārabahulo bhikṣuḥ pañcaughatīrṇas taratīha ṣaṣṭhaṃ /
children.translated_text: How should a <s>bhikṣu</s> dwell abundantly [in meditation] who has crossed the five floods and crosses the sixth here?

children.text: kathaṃdhyāyī vipulāṃ kāmatṛṣṇāṃ tīrṇo bhavaty apratilabdhayoktraḥ // Śag_4.1
children.translated_text: How should he meditate so that the vast craving for sense-pleasures is crossed over, [his mind] having found no hold? // <s>Śag</s> 4.1

body.text: praśrabdhakāyaḥ suvimuktacitto hy asaṃskurvan smṛtimān akopyaḥ

children.text: ājñāya dharmam avitarkadhyāyī kopaspṛhāstyānadoṣaiḥ viyuktaḥ // Śag_4.2
children.translated_text: having understood the <s>Dharma</s>, meditating without discursive thought, freed from the faults of anger, desire, and torpor — // <s>Śag</s> 4.2

children.text: evaṃvihārabahulo bhikṣuḥ pañcaughatīrṇas taratīha ṣaṣṭhaṃ /
children.translated_text: dwelling abundantly in this way, a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has crossed the five floods crosses the sixth here;

children.text: evaṃdhyāyī vipulāṃ kāmatṛṣṇāṃ tīrṇo bhavaty apratilabdhayoktraḥ // Śag_4.3
children.translated_text: meditating thus, the vast craving for sense-pleasures is crossed over, [the mind] having found no hold. // <s>Śag</s> 4.3

body.translated_text: With body tranquil, with mind well-liberated, not forming [new] formations, mindful, unshakeable,

children.text: nityotrasto hy ayaṃ loko nityodvignā iyaṃ prajā /
children.translated_text: This world is ever-frightened, this multitude is ever-anxious,

children.text: anutpanneṣu duḥkheṣu samutpanneṣu vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: whether in the face of sufferings not yet arisen or those already arisen;

children.text: yadi kiṃcid anutrastaṃ pṛṣṭa ācakṣva tan mama // Śag_5.1
children.translated_text: if there is anything free from fear, being asked, declare that to me. // <s>Śag</s> 5.1

children.text: nānyatra jñānatapaso nānyatrendriyanigrahāt /
children.translated_text: Nowhere other than through knowledge and austerity, nowhere other than through restraint of the senses,

children.text: nānyatra sarvasaṃtyāgān mokṣaṃ paśyāmi devate // Śag_5.2
children.translated_text: nowhere other than through the relinquishment of all — I see no liberation, O <s>devatā</s> (goddess). // <s>Śag</s> 5.2

children.text: cirasya bata paśyāmi brāhmaṇaṃ parinirvṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: At last indeed I see a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: sarvavairabhayātītaṃ tīrṇaṃ loke viṣaktikām // Śag_5.3
children.translated_text: who has gone beyond all enmity and fear, who has crossed the world's entanglement. // <s>Śag</s> 5.3

children.text: kenābhivarṇā janatā praṇītā mārgaś ca nairyāṇikataḥ prayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: By what is humanity distinguished and elevated? How is the path connected with the way of deliverance?

children.text: kutra sthitaḥ kutra ca śikṣamāṇo nāyaṃ martyaḥ paralokād bibheti // Śag_6.1
children.translated_text: Standing where and training in what does this mortal not fear the other world? // <s>Śag</s> 6.1

children.text: yaḥ śīlavāñ jñānavān bhāvitātmā samāhitaḥ smṛtimān ṛjugataś ca /
children.translated_text: One who is endowed with virtue, possessed of knowledge, with a cultivated self, concentrated, mindful, and of straightforward conduct —

children.text: sarve 'sya śokajvarathāḥ prahīṇāḥ samyaksmṛto yasya cittaṃ vimuktaṃ // Śag_6.2
children.translated_text: all his fevers of grief are abandoned; one whose mind is well-remembered and liberated — // <s>Śag</s> 6.2

children.text: tenābhivarṇā janatā praṇītā mārgaś ca nairyāṇikataḥ prayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: by that is humanity distinguished and elevated, and the path is connected with the way of deliverance;

children.text: atra sthitaḥ atra ca śikṣamāṇo nāyaṃ martyaḥ paralokād bibheti // Śag_6.3
children.translated_text: standing here and training in this, this mortal does not fear the other world. // <s>Śag</s> 6.3

children.text: kathaṃ yaśasvī bhavati kathaṃ bhavati bhogavān /
children.translated_text: How does one become renowned? How does one become wealthy?

children.text: kathaṃ kīrtim avāpnoti kathaṃ mitrāṇi vindati // Śag_7.1
children.translated_text: How does one attain fame? How does one find friends? // <s>Śag</s> 7.1

children.text: śīlād yaśasvī bhavati dānād bhavati bhogavān /
children.translated_text: Through virtue one becomes renowned; through generosity one becomes wealthy;

children.text: satyena kīrtim āpnoti dadan mitrāṇi vindati // Śag_7.2
children.translated_text: through truthfulness one attains fame; by giving, one finds friends. // <s>Śag</s> 7.2

children.text: kutaḥ sarā nivartante kutra vartma na vartate /
children.translated_text: From where do the streams turn back? Where does the path no longer proceed?

children.text: kutra duḥkhasukhaṃ loke niḥśeṣam uparudhyate // Śag_8.1
children.translated_text: Where in the world are pleasure and pain completely ceased? // <s>Śag</s> 8.1

children.text: cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ jihvā kāyo manas tathā /
children.translated_text: The eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, and the mind —

children.text: yatra nāma ca rūpaṃ ca niḥśeṣam uparuhyate // Śag_8.2
children.translated_text: where name and form completely cease, // <s>Śag</s> 8.2

children.text: tataḥ sarā nivartante tatra vartma na vartate /
children.translated_text: from there the streams turn back, there the path no longer proceeds,

children.text: tatra duḥkhasukhaṃ loke niḥśeṣam uparudhyate // Śag_8.3
children.translated_text: there in the world pleasure and pain completely cease. // <s>Śag</s> 8.3

children.text: kena svid oghaṃ tarati kenottarati cārṇavaṃ /
children.translated_text: By what does one cross the flood? By what does one cross the ocean?

children.text: duḥkhaṃ tyajati kena svit kena svit pariśudhyati // Śag_9.1
children.translated_text: By what does one abandon suffering? By what is one purified? // <s>Śag</s> 9.1

children.text: śraddhayā tarati hy ogham apramādena cārṇavaṃ /
children.translated_text: By faith one crosses the flood; by diligence one crosses the ocean;

children.text: vīryeṇa duḥkhaṃ tyajati prajñayā pariśudhyati // Śag_9.2
children.translated_text: by energy one abandons suffering; by wisdom one is purified. // <s>Śag</s> 9.2

children.text: ka etam oghaṃ tarati rātriṃdivam atandritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who crosses this flood, day and night unwearied?

children.text: anālambe 'pratiṣṭhe ca ko gaṃbhīre na sīdati // Śag_10.1
children.translated_text: Who does not sink in the deep, where there is no support and no foothold? // <s>Śag</s> 10.1

children.text: sarvataḥ śīlasaṃpannaḥ prajñāvān susamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is endowed with virtue in every respect, possessed of wisdom, well-concentrated,

children.text: adhyātmacintī smṛtimāṃs taratīmaṃ sudustaraṃ // Śag_10.2
children.translated_text: contemplating the inner [reality], mindful — such a one crosses this most difficult to cross. // <s>Śag</s> 10.2

children.text: viraktaḥ kāmasaṃjñābhyo rūpasaṃyojanātigaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dispassionate toward the perceptions of sense-desire, having transcended the fetters of form —

children.text: anālambe 'pratiṣṭhe ca sa gaṃbhīre na sīdati // Śag_10.3
children.translated_text: such a one does not sink in the deep, where there is no support and no foothold. // <s>Śag</s> 10.3

children.text: rāgadveṣau bhagavan kinnidānāv aratiratī romaharṣaḥ kuto 'yam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what is the origin of passion and hatred? Whence come aversion and delight and the bristling of hair?

children.text: kutaḥsamutthāś ca mano vitarkāḥ kumārakā dhātrīm ivāśrayante // Śag_11.1
children.translated_text: Whence do mental thoughts arise? Like boys clinging to a nurse, [they cling]. // <s>Śag</s> 11.1

children.text: snehajā ātmasaṃbhūtā nyagrodhaskandhakā yathā /
children.translated_text: Born of affection, arisen from oneself, like the shoots of a banyan tree,

children.text: pṛthagviṣaktāḥ kāmeṣu mālutā vā latā vane // Śag_11.2
children.translated_text: severally attached to sense-pleasures, like creepers spreading in the forest — // <s>Śag</s> 11.2

children.text: rāgaś ca dveṣaś ca itonidānāv aratiratī romaharṣaḥ ito 'yaṃ /
children.translated_text: Passion and hatred have their origin here; aversion, delight, and the bristling of hair — from here they come;

children.text: itaḥsamutthāś ca mano vitarkāḥ kumārakā dhātrīm ivāśrayante // Śag_11.3
children.translated_text: from here mental thoughts arise — like boys clinging to a nurse, [they cling]. // <s>Śag</s> 11.3

children.text: ye tān prajānanti yatonidānāṃs te tāṃ janā yakṣa vinodayanti /
children.translated_text: Those who understand whence these [passions] have their origin — those people, O <s>Yakṣa</s>, dispel them;

children.text: ta arṇavaṃ saṃpratarantīhaugham atīrṇapūrvam apunarbhavāya // Śag_11.4
children.translated_text: they cross here the ocean and the flood, never crossed before, for the sake of non-return to existence. // <s>Śag</s> 11.4

children.text: kāryam etad brāhmaṇena prahāṇam akilāsinā /
children.translated_text: This is what must be done by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — the abandonment, untiringly,

children.text: kāmānāṃ viprahāṇārthaṃ na hi kāṃkṣaty asau bhavaṃ // Śag_12.1
children.translated_text: [practiced] for the purpose of relinquishing sense-desires, for indeed such a one does not long for [further] existence. // <s>Śag</s> 12.1

body.text: sa kāryaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti kṛtārtho brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // Śag_12.2
body.translated_text: That is the task of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has accomplished it is called one whose task is done. // <s>Śag</s> 12.2

children.text: yāvan na gādhaṃ labhate na tīram āyūhate sarvagātraiḥ sa tāvat /
children.translated_text: So long as one does not reach the bottom or the shore, one strives with all limbs;

children.text: tīraṃ tu labdhveha saṃtiṣṭhati sthale nāyūhate pāragato nirucyate // Śag_12.3
children.translated_text: but having found the shore, one stands on firm ground and no longer strives — one who has gone beyond is so called. // <s>Śag</s> 12.3

children.text: eṣopamā dāmale brāhmaṇasya kṣīṇāsravo yo nipako dhyānalābhī /
children.translated_text: This is the simile, O <s>Dāmale</s>, of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — one whose outflows (<s>āśravas</s>) are destroyed, who is skilled, who has attained <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);

children.text: sarve 'sya śokajvarathāḥ prahīṇāḥ samyaksmṛto yasya cittaṃ vimuktam // Śag_12.4
children.translated_text: all his fevers of grief are abandoned; one whose mind is well-remembered and liberated. // <s>Śag</s> 12.4

body.text:
geya:
bhikṣo bhikṣo ogham atārṣīḥ /
āma devate /
anālambe 'pratiṣṭhe ogham atārṣīḥ /
āma devate /
yathā kathaṃ tvaṃ bhikṣo anālambe apratiṣṭhe ogham atārṣīḥ /
yathā yathāhaṃ devate āyūhāmi tathā tathā saṃsīdāmi / yathā yathā saṃsīdāmi tathā tathā saṃtiṣṭhe / yathā yathā saṃtiṣṭhe tathā tathā uhye / yathā yathāhaṃ devate nāyūhāmi tathā tathā na saṃsīdāmīti vistareṇa śuklapakṣo veditavya

children.text: ḥ

body.translated_text:
<s>Geya</s> (verse to be sung):
'O <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>bhikṣu</s>, you have crossed the flood!' — 'Yes, O <s>devatā</s>!' — 'You have crossed the flood where there is no support and no foothold!' — 'Yes, O <s>devatā</s>!' — 'How is it, <s>bhikṣu</s>, that you crossed the flood where there is no support and no foothold?' — 'Whenever I strove, O <s>devatā</s>, I sank; whenever I sank, I stood firm; whenever I stood firm, I was carried [forward]; whenever I did not strive, O <s>devatā</s>, I did not sink.' The bright half [of this teaching] should be understood in full detail.

children.text: kumārikāpraśnagāthā:
children.translated_text: Verses of the Maiden's Questions (<s>Kumārikāpraśnagāthā</s>):

children.text: eko 'raṇye prasṛto dhyāyase tvaṃ vittād vihīna uta vā prārthayānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alone in the forest, given to meditation, do you ponder — are you deprived of wealth or do you seek it?

children.text: grāmasya vā kiṃcanāgo nv akārṣīḥ kasmāj janena na karoṣi sakhyaṃ
children.translated_text: Or have you committed some offense against the village? Why do you not make friendship with people —

children.text: sakhyaṃ na saṃvidyate kena cit tava // Śag_14.1
children.translated_text: friendship is not found for you with anyone? // <s>Śag</s> 14.1

children.text: arthāprāptyā hṛdayasyeha śāntir jitveha senāṃ priyaśātarūpaṃ /
children.translated_text: Through the non-attainment of [worldly] goals there is peace of the heart here; having conquered the army of pleasant and delightful forms,

children.text: eko dhyāyī sukham asmy anvabhotsaṃ tasmād janena na karomi sakhyaṃ
children.translated_text: meditating alone, I have experienced happiness; therefore I do not make friendship with people —

children.text: sakhyaṃ na saṃvidyate kena cid mama // Śag_14.2
children.translated_text: friendship is not found for me with anyone. // <s>Śag</s> 14.2

children.text: anityā bata saṃskārā utpādavyayadharmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas, impermanent are formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), subject to the law of arising and passing away;

children.text: utpadya hi nirudhyante teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukham // Śag_15 (cf. Uv 1.3)
children.translated_text: having arisen, they cease — their stilling is bliss. // <s>Śag</s> 15 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 1.3)

body.text:
apramādo 'mṛtapadaṃ pramādo mṛtyunaḥ padaṃ /
apramattā na mriyante pramattās tu sadā mṛtā

children.text: ḥ
vitarkapramathitasya dehinas tīvrarāgasya śubhānudarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the embodied being shaken by discursive thoughts, of intense passion, seeing the attractive in things —

children.text: bhūyas tṛṣṇā vivardhate sā gāḍhīkurute 'sya bandhanaṃ // Śag_17 (cf. Uv 3.1)
children.translated_text: craving grows all the more, and it tightens the bondage for that one. // <s>Śag</s> 17 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 3.1)

children.text: dharmasthaṃ śīlasaṃpannaṃ hrīmantaṃ satyavādinaṃ /
children.translated_text: One who stands in the <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with virtue, possessed of modesty, speaking truth —

children.text: ātmanaḥ priyakartāraṃ taṃ janaḥ kurute priyaṃ // Śag_18 (cf. Uv 5.24)
children.translated_text: one who does what is dear to oneself — such a person the people hold dear. // <s>Śag</s> 18 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 5.24)

children.text: yat pareṣūpanidhyāyet karma dṛṣṭveha pāpakam /
children.translated_text: Having observed evil <s>karma</s> in others here,

children.text: ātmanā tan na kurvīta karmabaddho hi pāpakaḥ // Śag_19 (cf. Uv 9.6)
children.translated_text: one should not do that oneself, for the evildoer is bound by <s>karma</s>. // <s>Śag</s> 19 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 9.6)

children.text: subhāṣitaṃ hy uttamam āhur āryāḥ priyaṃ vaden nāpriyaṃ tad dvitīyaṃ /
children.translated_text: The noble ones declare well-spoken speech to be the foremost; the second is: speak what is pleasant, not what is unpleasant;

children.text: satyaṃ vaden nānṛtaṃ tat tṛtīyaṃ dharmaṃ vaden nādharmaṃ tat caturtham // Śag_20 (cf. Uv 8.11)
children.translated_text: the third is: speak truth, not falsehood; the fourth is: speak <s>Dharma</s>, not <s>adharma</s>. // <s>Śag</s> 20 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 8.11)

children.text: śraddhātha hrīḥ śīlam athāpi dānaṃ dharmā ime satpuruṣapraśastāḥ /
children.translated_text: Faith, and modesty, virtue, and also generosity — these are the <s>dharmas</s> praised by the good;

children.text: etaṃ hi mārgaṃ divigaṃ vadanti etena vai gacchati devalokam // Śag_21 (cf. Uv 10.1)
children.translated_text: this indeed they call the path leading to heaven; by this one goes to the world of the <s>devas</s>. // <s>Śag</s> 21 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 10.1)

children.text: śrutvā dharmaṃ vijānāti śrutvā pāpān nivartate /
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, one understands; having heard, one turns away from evil;

children.text: śrutvā anarthaṃ tyajati śrutvā prāpnoti nirvṛtim // Śag_22 (cf. Uv 22.6)
children.translated_text: having heard, one abandons what is harmful; having heard, one attains peace (<s>nirvṛti</s>). // Śag 22 (cf. Uv 22.6)

children.text: ākāśasamo na lipyate indrakīlapratimo na kaṃpate /
children.translated_text: Like space, he is not stained; like <s>Indra</s>'s pillar, he does not tremble;

children.text: hrada iva samupetakardame saṃsāre ramate na paṇḍitaḥ // Śag_23 (cf. Uv 17.12)
children.translated_text: like a lake with settled mud, the wise one does not delight in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Śag 23 (cf. Uv 17.12)

children.text: ye rūpeṇa pramiṇvanti māṃ ghoṣeṇānuyānti ca /
children.translated_text: Those who judge me by form, those who follow me by voice,

children.text: cchandarāgavaśopetā na mā jānanti te janāḥ // Śag_24.1 (cf. Uv 22.12)
children.translated_text: those people, under the power of desire and passion, do not truly know me. // Śag 24.1 (cf. Uv 22.12)

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca vijānāti bahirdhā ca na paśyati /
children.translated_text: One who knows the inner (<s>adhyātma</s>) but does not see the outer —

children.text: adhyātmaphaladarśī yaḥ sa vai ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.2 (cf. Uv 22.13)
children.translated_text: that one, seeing only inner results, is led by mere sound. // Śag 24.2 (cf. Uv 22.13)

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca na jānāti bahirdhā ca vipaśyati /
children.translated_text: One who does not know the inner but sees the outer —

children.text: bahirdhāphaladarśī yaḥ so 'pi ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.3 (cf. Uv 22.14)
children.translated_text: that one, seeing only outer results, is also led by mere sound. // Śag 24.3 (cf. Uv 22.14)

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca na jānāti bahirdhā ca na paśyati /
children.translated_text: One who does not know the inner and does not see the outer —

children.text: samantāvaraṇo bālaḥ so 'pi ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.4 (cf. Uv 22.15)
children.translated_text: that fool, obscured on all sides, is also led by mere sound. // Śag 24.4 (cf. Uv 22.15)

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca vijānāti bahirdhā ca vipaśyati /
children.translated_text: One who knows the inner and also sees the outer —

children.text: dhīro niḥsaraṇaprajño na sa ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.5 (cf. Uv 22.16)
children.translated_text: that steadfast one, wise in the way of liberation, is not led by mere sound. // Śag 24.5 (cf. Uv 22.16)

body.translated_text: Heedfulness (<s>apramāda</s>) is the path to the deathless; heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless are as if always dead.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe adhipatau rājñi rajyamāne rajasvalaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the sixth ruler reigns as king, the passionate one is full of passion;

children.text: arajasy arajā bhavati rakto bālo nirucyate // Śag_25 (cf. Uv 16.22)
children.translated_text: in the passionless, one becomes free of passion — [but only] the deluded fool is called 'attached.' // Śag 25 (cf. Uv 16.22)

children.text: nagaram asthiprākāraṃ snāyumāṃsānulepanaṃ /
children.translated_text: A city with walls of bones, plastered with sinews and flesh,

children.text: yatra rāgaś ca dveṣaś ca māno mrakṣaś ca gāhate // Śag_26 (cf. Uv 16.23)
children.translated_text: where passion, hatred, pride, and hypocrisy take hold. // Śag 26 (cf. Uv 16.23)

children.text: kūrmaḥ svake 'ṅgāni yathā kapāle bhikṣur nidadhyān manaso vitarkāni /
children.translated_text: Just as a tortoise [draws] its limbs into its shell, so should a <s>bhikṣu</s> withdraw the thoughts of the mind.

children.text: aniśrito 'nyān aviheṭhamānaḥ parinirvṛto nāpavadeta kaṃ cit // Śag_27 (cf. Uv 26.1)
children.translated_text: Independent, not harming others, fully at peace — one should not speak ill of anyone. // Śag 27 (cf. Uv 26.1)

children.text: tulyam atulyaṃ ca saṃbhavaṃ bhavasaṃskāram avāsṛjan muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having let go of the equal and unequal, of becoming and the formations of existence, the sage,

children.text: adhyātmarataḥ samāhita abhinat kośam ivāṇḍasaṃbhavaḥ // Śag_28 (cf. Uv 26.30)
children.translated_text: delighting inwardly, concentrated, has broken through the shell like one born from an egg. // Śag 28 (cf. Uv 26.30)

children.text: nāsti kāmasamaḥ paṃko nāsti dveṣasamo grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no mire like desire; there is no grip like hatred;

children.text: nāsti mohasamaṃ jālaṃ nāsti tṛṣṇāsamā nadī // Śag_29 (cf. Uv 29.37)
children.translated_text: there is no net like delusion; there is no river like craving. // Śag 29 (cf. Uv 29.37)

children.text: ākāśe vai padaṃ nāsti śramaṇo nāsti bāhyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: In space, indeed, there is no path; there is no <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant) outside [the teaching];

children.text: prapañcābhiratā bālā niṣprapañcās tathāgatāḥ // Śag_30 (cf. Uv 29.38)
children.translated_text: the foolish delight in conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>); the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are free from proliferation. // Śag 30 (cf. Uv 29.38)

body.text: sthitiḥ prapaṃcāś ca na santi yasya yaḥ sa

children.text: ṃ
dānaṃ parighaṃ cātivṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: gone beyond the impediment of [selfish] giving —

children.text: taṃ nistṛṣṇaṃ muniṃ carantaṃ na vijānāti sadevako 'pi lokaḥ // Śag_31 (cf. Uv 29.51)
children.translated_text: that desireless sage, wandering [free], is not known even by the world with its gods. // Śag 31 (cf. Uv 29.51)

children.text:
yasya vitarkā vidhūpitā adhyātmam avikalpitā aśeṣaṃ /
saṃgaṃ so 'tītya rūpasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: One whose discursive thoughts are dispelled, who is inwardly free from all conceptualization,

children.text: ṃ
caturyogāpagato na jātim eti // Śag_32 (cf. Uv 29.56)
children.translated_text: having passed beyond attachment and the perception of form, gone beyond the four bonds — such a one does not come to birth. // Śag 32 (cf. Uv 29.56)

children.text: dadataḥ puṇyaṃ pravardhate vairaṃ saṃyamato na cīyate /
children.translated_text: For one who gives, merit increases; for one who restrains himself, enmity does not accumulate;

children.text: kuśalī prajahāti pāpakaṃ kleśānāṃ kṣayatas tu nirvṛtaḥ // Śag_33 (cf. Uv 28.2)
children.translated_text: the skillful one abandons evil; through the destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), one is at peace. // Śag 33 (cf. Uv 28.2)

children.text: sarvapāpasyākaraṇaṃ kuśalasyopasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: Not doing any evil, the accomplishment of what is wholesome,

children.text: svacittaparyavadamanam etaṃ buddhānuśāsanaṃ // Śag_34 (cf. Uv 28.1)
children.translated_text: the purification of one's own mind — this is the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Śag 34 (cf. Uv 28.1)

children.text: durnigrahasya laghuno yatrakāmanipātinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is difficult to restrain, light, and alights wherever it wishes;

children.text: cittasya dāmanaṃ sādhu cittaṃ dāntaṃ sukhāvaham // Śag_35 (cf. Uv 31.1)
children.translated_text: the taming of the mind is good — a tamed mind brings happiness. // Śag 35 (cf. Uv 31.1)

children.text: cittanimittasya kovidaḥ pravivekasya ca vindate rasaṃ /
children.translated_text: One skilled in the signs of the mind finds the taste of seclusion;

children.text: dhyāyī nipakaḥ pratismṛto bhuṃkte prītisukhaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ // Śag_36 (cf. Uv 31.51)
children.translated_text: the meditator, watchful, mindful, enjoys the bliss of joy that is beyond the material. // Śag 36 (cf. Uv 31.51)

children.text:
aśilpajīvī laghur ātmakāmo jitendriyaḥ sarvato vipramuktaḥ /
anokasārī hy amamo nirāśaḥ kāmān prahāyaikacaro yas sa bhikṣu
children.translated_text: Living without craft, light, self-controlled, with senses conquered, everywhere completely liberated, dwelling without attachment, without possessiveness, without expectation — having abandoned sensual desires, wandering alone — that one is a <s>bhikṣu</s>

children.text: ḥ

// Śag_37 (cf. Uv 32.5)
dūraṃga
children.translated_text: // Śag 37 (cf. Uv 32.5) Far-wandering,

children.text: ma
m ekacaram aśarīraṃ guhāśayaṃ /
children.translated_text: solitary, bodiless, lying in the cave [of the heart] —

children.text: damayati durdamaṃ cittaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ bravīmy ahaṃ // Śag_38 (cf. Uv 33.55)
children.translated_text: whoever tames the difficult-to-tame mind — that one I call a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // Śag 38 (cf. Uv 33.55)

body.translated_text: For whom there exist neither fixation nor conceptual proliferations, who has

children.text: pārāyaṇeṣv ajitapraśnaḥ:
children.translated_text: From the <s>Pārāyaṇa</s>, the Question of <s>Ajita</s>:

children.text: kenāyaṃ nivṛto lokaḥ kenāyaṃ na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: By what is this world enveloped? By what does it not shine forth?

children.text: kiṃ cābhilepanaṃ brūṣe kiṃ ca tasya mahad bhayam // Śag_39.1
children.translated_text: What do you call its defilement, and what is its great fear? // Śag 39.1

children.text: avidyānivṛto lokaḥ pramādān na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: The world is enveloped by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); through heedlessness it does not shine forth;

children.text: jalpābhilepanaṃ brūmi duḥkhaṃ tasya mahad bhayaṃ // Śag_39.2
children.translated_text: I call idle talk (<s>jalpa</s>) its defilement, and suffering is its great fear. // Śag 39.2

children.text: sravanti sarvataḥ srotāḥ srotasāṃ kiṃ nivāraṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Streams flow everywhere — what is the restraint for the streams?

children.text: srotasāṃ saṃvaraṃ brūhi kena srotaḥ pidhīyate // Śag_39.3
children.translated_text: Tell me the dam for the streams — by what are the streams blocked? // Śag 39.3

children.text: yāni srotāṃsi lokasya smṛtiḥ teṣāṃ nivāraṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Whatever streams there are in the world, mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is their restraint;

children.text: srotasāṃ saṃvaraṃ brūmi prajñayā hi pidhīyate // Śag_39.4
children.translated_text: I declare the dam for the streams — by wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) they are blocked. // Śag 39.4

children.text: prajñāyāś ca smṛteś caiva nāmarūpasya sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of wisdom and mindfulness, and of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) entirely —

children.text: ācakṣva pṛṣṭa etan me kutraitad uparudhyate // Śag_39.5
children.translated_text: tell me, being asked this: where does this cease? // Śag 39.5

children.text: prajñā caiva smṛtiś caiva nāmarūpaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wisdom and mindfulness, and name-and-form entirely —

children.text: vijñānasya nirodhād dhi atraitad uparudhyate // Śag_39.6
children.translated_text: through the cessation of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), here this ceases. // Śag 39.6

children.text: kathaṃ smṛtasya carato vijñānam uparudhyate /
children.translated_text: For one who goes about mindfully, how does consciousness cease?

children.text: ācakṣva pṛṣṭa etan me yathātatham asaṃśayaḥ // Śag_39.7
children.translated_text: Tell me, being asked this, the truth of the matter without doubt. // Śag 39.7

children.text: adhyātaṃ ca bahirdhā ca vedanāṃ nābhinandataḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who does not delight in feelings (<s>vedanā</s>), whether internal or external —

children.text: evaṃ smṛtasya carato vijñānam uparudhyate // Śag_39.8
children.translated_text: for one who goes about thus mindfully, consciousness ceases. // Śag 39.8

body.text: ye ca saṃkhyātadharmāṇo ye ca śaikṣāḥ pṛ

children.text: tha
gvidhāḥ /
children.translated_text: of various kinds —

children.text: teṣāṃ me nipakasyeryāṃ pṛṣṭaḥ prabrūhi mārṣa // Śag_39.9
children.translated_text: tell me, sir, being asked, the conduct of the wise among them. // Śag 39.9

children.text: kāmeṣu nābhigṛdhyeta manasānāvilo bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should not be greedy for sensual pleasures; the mind should be untroubled;

children.text: kuśalaḥ sarvadharmeṣu smṛto bhikṣuḥ parivrajet // Śag_39.10
children.translated_text: skilled in all <s>dharmas</s>, a mindful <s>bhikṣu</s> should wander forth. // Śag 39.10

body.translated_text: Those who have comprehended the <s>dharmas</s>, and those who are in training (<s>śaikṣas</s>),

children.text: arthavargīyeṣu kāmān ārabhya gāthā:
children.translated_text: From the <s>Arthavargīya</s>, verses concerning sensual desires:

children.text: kāmān kāmāyamānasya tasya cet tat samṛdhyati /
children.translated_text: When one who desires pleasures — if that [desire] of his is fulfilled,

children.text: addhā prītamanā bhavati labdhvā martyo yad īpsitaṃ // Śag_40.1
children.translated_text: then a mortal, having obtained what he wished for, is indeed glad at heart. // Śag 40.1

children.text: tasya cet kāmāyamānasya chandajātasya jaṃtunaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for that being who desires pleasures, in whom desire has arisen,

children.text: te kāmāḥ parihīyaṃte śalyaviddha iva rūpyate // Śag_40.2
children.translated_text: when those pleasures diminish, he suffers as though pierced by an arrow. // Śag 40.2

children.text: yaḥ kāmāṃ parivarjayati sarpasyeva śirāt padaṃ /
children.translated_text: Whoever avoids sensual desires, as [one avoids stepping on] a serpent's head —

children.text: sa imāṃ viṣaktikāṃ loke smṛtaḥ samativartate // Śag_40.3
children.translated_text: that mindful one transcends this attachment in the world. // Śag 40.3

children.text: kṣetravastuhiraṇ@yaṃ ca gavāśvamaṇikuṇḍalaṃ /
children.translated_text: Fields, property, gold,

children.text: striyo dāsān pṛthakkāmān yo naro hy abhigṛdhyati // Śag_40.4
children.translated_text: cattle, horses, jewels, earrings, women, servants — whoever craves these separate pleasures, // Śag 40.4

body.text: abalaṃ vā balīyāṃso mṛdnaṃty enaṃ parisravā

children.text: ḥ
tata enaṃ duḥkham anveti bhinnāṃ nāvam ivodakaṃ // Śag_40.5
children.translated_text: and then suffering follows him, as water [enters] a broken boat. // Śag 40.5

children.text: yasya tv etat samucchinnaṃ tālamastakavad dhataṃ /
children.translated_text: But for whom this [craving] has been cut off, destroyed like the crown of a palm tree —

children.text: śokās tasya nivartante udabindur iva puṣkarāt // Śag_40.6 (cf. Uv 10.13ab und 3.10cd)
children.translated_text: sorrows turn away from that one, like a water-drop from a lotus leaf. // Śag 40.6 (cf. Uv 10.13ab and 3.10cd)

body.translated_text: the stronger [forces of defilement] crush that weak one,

children.text: bhadraikarāgāthā (bhadragarātrīya, bhadrakarātriya):
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhaddekaratta-gāthā</s> (Verse on the Auspicious One-Night):

children.text: atītaṃ nānvāgamayen na pratikāṃkṣed anāgataṃ /
children.translated_text: One should not chase after the past, nor long for the future;

children.text: pratyutpannāś ca ye dharmās tatra tatra vipaśyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: as for the <s>dharmas</s> present [right now], one should see clearly into each of them.

children.text: asaṃhāryam asaṃkṣobhyaṃ tad vidvān anubṛṃhayet // Śag_41.1
children.translated_text: What cannot be taken away, what cannot be shaken — the wise one should cultivate that. // Śag 41.1
